goal: Build Phase 6 (Self-Evolving Harness): failure store, categorization, skill proposal, candidate skill store, regression-gated promote/reject, skill metadata -- demonstrated end-to-end with real Gazebo physics data, not fabricated examples.

pipeline_demonstration.step_1_failure_store: harness/failure_store.py scanned tasks/*/result.json, found 3 failures (BENCH-001, BENCH-003, CTRL-003), wrote harness/failure_store.jsonl
pipeline_demonstration.step_2_categorization: harness/categorize_failures.py grouped BENCH-001 and BENCH-003 (both: plant-definition file changed, controller-model file NOT changed) into category 'plant-model-inconsistency' -- correctly excluded CTRL-003 (different files touched) and BENCH-002 (explicitly changed linear_model.py, i.e. the fix, not the failure)
pipeline_demonstration.step_3_skill_proposal: harness/propose_skill.py generated harness/skills/candidates/SKILL-CONTROL-MODEL-CONSISTENCY.yaml once evidence reached 2, matching project_plan.md section 11.1's exact schema (id/trigger/procedure/reason/evidence) plus section 13's lifecycle metadata (status=candidate, created_from, activation_count=0, etc)
pipeline_demonstration.step_4_5_benchmark_data: BENCH-001 (m2 1.0->1.4, no model regen) and BENCH-003 (L1 1.0->1.3, no model regen) both real Gazebo LQR/nominal_balance N=3 runs, both 0/3 pass_rate, both with a catastrophic run-3 failure NOT seen in a same-session matched-plant control (also 0/3, but no instability, no torque saturation, no zero-torque event -- see control_comparison below). BENCH-002 applied the skill's procedure (regenerate linear_model.py to m2=1.4) against BENCH-001's exact scenario.
pipeline_demonstration.step_6_promotion_gate: harness/promote_skill.py compared BENCH-001 (baseline, pass_rate=0.0) vs BENCH-002 (candidate, pass_rate=0.0) -> REJECT (candidate did not beat baseline). Skill correctly stayed in skills/candidates/ with an auditable rejection note appended (not silently dropped, not force-promoted).

control_comparison.purpose: isolate whether BENCH-001/003's failures were caused by the deliberate mismatch or by CTRL-003's already-documented pre-existing LQR/nominal_balance run-to-run physics variance

matched_control.note: 0/3 like the mismatched conditions, but ALL 3 runs had reasonable overshoot (~16 deg) and torque well under limits (~22/9 Nm) -- fails only on the settling_time_q1 criterion, the same borderline issue already known from CTRL-003/004, not catastrophic

mismatch_mass_BENCH-001.note: run 3 catastrophic: overshoot 223.7/83.7 deg, BOTH actuators saturated at their torque limits (60/30 Nm)

mismatch_length_BENCH-003.note: run 3 catastrophic: overshoot 539.1/282.3 deg, ZERO effective torque -- a different failure signature than BENCH-001's saturation

control_comparison.conclusion: the raw pass_rate metric alone cannot separate 'mismatch effect' from 'pre-existing variance' here, since even the matched control already fails 0/3 on the settling-time criterion. But the qualitative failure mode differs cleanly: catastrophic instability (saturation or zero-torque) appeared in BOTH mismatch conditions and in NEITHER the matched control's 3 runs observed this session -- real evidence the mismatch has a genuine physical effect, even though it isn't visible in pass_rate alone at this scenario's existing near-universal settling-time failure rate.

notes: The pipeline itself works correctly end-to-end and made the right call (REJECT) given the actual data -- that correctness, not a successful skill promotion, is what this task's acceptance criteria required. The candidate skill's REJECT does not mean plant/model consistency is unimportant (control_comparison shows the mismatch is real and physically meaningful); it means this specific fix (regenerating only the linear model's mass/length parameters, same Q/R weights, same disturbance magnitude, N=3 sample) was not demonstrated to recover pass_rate in this test. Left as an open engineering question for later, same as CTRL-003's still-unresolved variance and the still-unresolved LQI gain-convergence issue: possible next steps if this skill is revisited are (1) larger N per benchmark condition to separate the mismatch's effect from background variance more cleanly, (2) re-tuning Q/R (not just the model) as part of the skill's procedure when the mismatch is large, (3) checking whether BENCH-003's zero-torque run-3 failure is a genuine physics effect of the length change or an unrelated controller-node/DDS hiccup (a zero-torque failure mode was also seen with NO mismatch at all in CTRL-004's PD testing).
